ai_review.summary: Pristine soundboard‑style recording with crisp, robust audio captures a standout show featuring Easy Wind, Minglewood Blues and Working Man’s Dead material.
ai_review.review: The tape delivers an unusually clear and full‑bodied sound that lets Jerry’s Gibson SG guitar shine throughout the set, while Bob Weir’s vocals and solos stand out on tracks like Easy Wind and Good Lovin'. The performance is highlighted by tight renditions of Working Man’s Dead/American Beauty songs and a fiery Minglewood Blues, though the second set shows some uneven moments (e.g., a flat Casey Jones). Overall the musical quality outweighs the few speed/pitch quirks noted in later analyses.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews are 5‑star praising both performance and audio fidelity; only a few note minor speed issues or weaker moments, resulting in an overall high rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Reviewers repeatedly describe the sound as pristine, crisp, robust and well‑balanced; stage mics capture deep low end and hall reverberation. A few later comments note occasional pitch/speed inconsistencies and minor glitches that have been partially cleaned up.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is strong, dominated by Working Man’s Dead/American Beauty material with tight vocals and inventive guitar work. The second set has high points (Easy Wind, Good Lovin') but some uneven stretches, notably a flat Casey Jones.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for his fiery Gibson SG tone, continuous improvisations, and inventive riffs throughout the show.
band_member_comments.Phil: Mentioned only in passing regarding a bass call‑out during Beat It On Down The Line; no strong praise or criticism.
band_member_comments.Bob: Highlighted for solid vocals and lead work on Easy Wind and Friend of the Devil; described as ‘well‑recorded’ and “fantastic”.
band_member_comments.Drums: A splice before the Good Lovin' jam is noted; otherwise drums are described as hot and supportive.
